**(1) First message to the user**

The ticket's owner-column row conflicts with the code. `src/export/csv.ts:40` defines the only column contract as `const tableColumns = ["title", "status"];`, and the gather draft says the export reuses those table column definitions. So an export built on that contract has no owner column. I found no owner field anywhere in the gathered evidence. The design continues on that corrected fact, and you can override it in your reply.

Two other premises could not be checked. First, the existing paging path is not in the gathered files. Second, no timing measurement exists for the row "The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s". I'm carrying both as unverified premises into Open Questions rather than stopping on them.

The framing holds: checked the column contract at `src/export/csv.ts:40`, the gather draft's finding that the reports page renders a table with no export action, and the serializer's reuse of the table column definitions. The paging and timing dependencies behind the 10k-row row could not be checked from the fixtures. No evidence shows the export is already shipped or misdiagnosed. The `## Issue tracker` override names `repo: acme/widgets`, and the ticket has no repo groups, so all three rows belong to this repo.

Ticket row "The export includes the owner column." contradicts the column contract at `src/export/csv.ts:40`, which lists only title and status. How should this row be handled?
A) in-scope - the export adds an owner column after the reused table columns, sourced from the report's owner data
B) deviates: the export follows the table contract and ships title and status only
C) deferred: owner column tracked in a follow-up ticket
D) repair the ticket - /skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77 row "The export includes the owner column." - `src/export/csv.ts:40` defines columns as title and status, with no owner
Recommendation: A - the owner column is part of the ticket contract and ships in this gauntlet as a column-list extension on the existing serializer, with the owner data source recorded as an open question.

---

**(2) Approaches message**

*(Recorded answers: the button sits beside the report title; reuse the existing CSV serializer and paging. The owner row stays at its default `in-scope` disposition pending your answer to the cut question.)*

These implicit dependencies are recorded as missing or not checkable:

- **Owner data source: missing.** The lookup was `src/export/csv.ts:40`. It holds only `["title", "status"]`, and no gathered file names an owner field. Where the owner value comes from goes into Open Questions.
- **Existing paging path: not checkable.** You named it as the thing to reuse, but no paging file is in the gathered evidence. Its location stays unverified until I read it in the next step.
- **10k-row timing measurement: not checkable.** No test or harness that times an export appears in the gathered files. How the under-60s row is measured goes into Open Questions.

**Recommended: reuse the serializer with a column parameter.** The approaches differ on where the owner column is defined.

The Export CSV button beside the report title calls the existing serializer in `src/export/csv.ts` through the existing paging. The serializer gains a column-list parameter. The export passes the table columns plus `owner`. The table's own column list is left unchanged, so the page looks the same.

This is the reuse-only option: no new serializer, only a parameter on the shared one. The blast radius is every other caller of the serializer. They keep today's output by defaulting the parameter to `tableColumns`.

Removes: none
Adds: Export CSV button in the reports page component beside the title; a columns parameter on the `src/export/csv.ts` serializer (defaulting to `tableColumns`); the `owner` column entry passed by the export call site; an export test file covering the button, the owner column, and the 10k-row run
Pattern: follows the serializer's reuse of the table column definitions at `src/export/csv.ts:40`, extending the shared path instead of copying it.

**Alternative: put owner in the shared column contract.** This drops the ask's implicit assumption that owner is an export-only column. It adds `owner` to `tableColumns` itself, so the table and the export stay a single contract. The trade-off is that the reports table also gains a visible owner column, which no ticket row asks for. It also affects every consumer of `tableColumns`.

Removes: none
Adds: Export CSV button beside the title; `"owner"` in `tableColumns` at `src/export/csv.ts:40`; an owner cell in the reports table; an export test file
Pattern: follows the single column contract at `src/export/csv.ts:40` and keeps table and export identical, at the cost of changing the page beyond the ticket.

**Not viable: a separate export-only column list beside the serializer.** It would create a second column path beside the one `src/export/csv.ts:40` already owns. The parameter in the recommended approach gives the same result without that duplication.

**What would flip the recommendation:** if reading the owner data source shows owner already belongs to the table's row model and product wants it visible on the page, the shared-contract alternative wins, because it keeps one contract.
